links.note: OVERWRITE of 31613 'Spots all in a line', which is how Jody knew the fawn was a buck. His thoughts drifting back to the fawn is the extract's opening, alongside Penny's praise in 31607; the set has no concept for that first line on its own.

OVERWRITE of 31612 'Jody gives up his milk', which is his mother's condition for consenting. Mill-wheel's offer of a ride is the Mill-wheel exchange, 31614, which is also where Jody decides to go alone.
OVERWRITE of 31618 'A carried fawn will follow', which happens after the fawn is found. Fearing he had mistaken his direction belongs to the trek to the clearing, held here as 31615.
OVERWRITE of 31620 'Nothing to be made of a gourd', which is the failed feeding at home. The fawn smelling sweetly of grass is in 31617, with the soft sleek skin he strokes.

OVERWRITE of 31608 'The doe that saved Penny', which is the snakebite remedy. His heart thumping at the marvel of the fawn's acceptance is the contact of 31617; 31618 is the later proof that it would follow him.
